data.sourceText:
“One Minutes” (5 per side)

H.R. 8884 – Removing Barriers to Work for Disabled Americans Act (Rep. Scott (GA) – Ways and Means) (Subject to a Rule)

This bill would reauthorize the Social Security Administration’s (SSA) ability to conduct demonstration projects to test Social Security Disability Insurance (SSDI) program changes for beneficiaries attempting to return to work. The SSDI program currently provides monthly benefits to people who are unable to or are very limited in their ability to work.

While previous reauthorizations of the SSDI demonstration authority involved close coordination between Congress and SSA to better understand the administration’s planned use of this authority, that has not been the case for this bill. In fact, when asked at Committee markup if the administration has provided a list of planned experiments, Committee Republicans stated they are “not aware of any such lists." Despite House Republicans' deceptive phrasing about one’s income not decreasing, this bill does not include language shielding program participants from potential benefit cuts. In President Trump’s first term, he proposed cutting approximately $50 billion over 10 years from disability benefits by using SSA demonstration authorities, and his current administration has considered a rule that would take away SSDI benefits from older, severely disabled workers by implementing barriers to make it harder to attain their benefits. Without prior knowledge of how SSA intends to use this demonstration authority and with inadequate guardrails to constrain its use, this bill could allow the administration to wreak havoc on disability benefits. 

Further, after the Trump Administration has slashed SSA staff and thrown the agency into a customer service crisis, House Republicans are choosing to change current law to require SSA to dip into its customer service budget to fund the administrative costs of SSDI demonstrations. 

At a time when Americans are facing the highest inflation rate in three years, House Republicans risk giving the administration the ability to cut SSDI benefits as they see fit. House Democrats will continue to work on solutions to improve Social Security without endangering those who need it most.

Ranking Member Neal strongly opposes this bill.

The Rule, which was adopted on Tuesday, provides for one hour of debate equally divided and controlled by the Chair and Ranking Member of the Committee on Ways and Means or their respective designees.
